### Entity invariants — enforce these
- Reuse or extend `Notification`: Every Notification created through the repository has a generated `id` (string) and `createdAt` (Date) assigned by the database — the caller supplies only `recipientId`, `type`, `title`, `message`, `relatedEntityType`, `relatedEntityId`, `status`, and `readAt`.
- Reuse or extend `Notification`: A Notification's `status` transitions from `pending` (on creation by a notify* method) to `read` (via `markAsRead`). The `readAt` field is `null` until the notification is marked as read, at which point it is set to the current timestamp.
- Reuse or extend `Notification`: When created via a `notify*` service method, `relatedEntityType` is always `'leave_request'` and `relatedEntityId` is always the `leaveRequest.id` — notifications are always tied to a specific leave request.
### Interface contract — expose these operations (their shape is yours)
- INotificationRepository.create — Must return the fully-hydrated Notification (with id and createdAt). If the database insert fails, the error propagates to the caller — the repository does not catch or transform it.
